hypotheses.name: specification insufficiency
hypotheses.claim: the prompt does not contain enough information to deduce the correct expected value
supporting_signature: base and SFT both low on P(correct oracle | disc)
Probe A: only A4 (behavioural evidence) raises the conditional oracle rate; A1-A3 do not
weakening_signature: Probe A: A1/A2/A3 raise the conditional oracle rate by >= 5 points

evidence.why: not identifiable from retained outputs; needs a Phase 3 probe

A3 (non-revealing type/length) - A0: base -0.42 [-3.125, 2.292], SFT +1.25 [-1.458, 3.958]; A4 (fixed code shown) - A0: base +6.04 [3.125, 9.167], SFT +5.21 [2.292, 8.333]. Specification contributes directionally (A4) but is not the dominant limit: accuracy with the fixed implementation shown is only 0.331 (base) / 0.338 (SFT).
evidence.withdrawn_reason: described A3 as non-revealing context; A3 is an oracle-derived partial hint

evidence.why: Non-revealing invariants (A3) do not help at 1.5B or 7B (7B A3-A0 +1.25 [-1.04, 3.54]). The fixed implementation (A4) helps modestly at 1.5B (+6.0) but strongly at 7B (+19.38 [14.79, 24.17]): once execution reasoning is adequate, the production information (buggy code + one-line specification) becomes the binding limit.
evidence.withdrawn_reason: undeclared status 'scale_dependent'; treated A4 as specification evidence

evidence.why: A3 (oracle-derived type/length hint) did not measurably help at 1.5B or 7B: this particular hint was insufficient, nothing more. A4 (access to the fixed implementation) helps modestly at 1.5B and strongly at 7B (+19.4, CI [14.8, 24.2]); that shows access to the correct implementation improves prediction, not that the natural-language specification is under-specified. A1/A2 were not run, so richer public context remains untested.

hypotheses.name: objective mismatch
hypotheses.claim: next-token imitation of whole tests does not optimise oracle correctness; it shifts input choice more than value prediction
hypotheses.mediator: P(disc | execute) up and P(correct oracle | disc) flat or down under SFT
supporting_signature: Phase 2: SFT raises P(disc|execute) while P(correct oracle|disc) falls
Phase 4: oracle-only or verifier-filtered supervision raises P(correct oracle|disc) >= 5 points where arm-A-style SFT does not
weakening_signature: Phase 2: SFT raises P(correct oracle | disc)
hypotheses.decisive_test: Phase 2, then a Phase 4 single-factor arm

evidence.why: P(disc|execute) +4.37 points, CI [1.9382, 6.9406]. The frozen signature (P(correct oracle|disc) falls) holds unstratified: -13.85, CI [-22.5204, -4.7957]. Stratified by assertion form (added after the first look), exact-value accuracy on discriminating inputs moves -4.25, CI [-11.0905, 2.6711]: SFT neither measurably damaged nor improved value prediction (an improvement of >= 5 points is excluded). Imitation transferred assertion form and input choice, not the value. Causal support needs a Phase 4 single-factor arm
input choice and assertion form moved under imitation; no value-prediction improvement is demonstrated. Causal support requires a Phase 4 arm.

fixed-input value prediction, all items, A0: SFT-base +1.46 [-2.5, 5.625]: no value-prediction improvement demonstrated from SFT on its own supervision distribution, including literal training targets; imitation moved form and input choice (Phase 2), not values.
evidence.withdrawn_reason: its fixed-input claim ('no improvement ... including literal training targets') is schema-dependent in the exposed strata

evidence.why: Rests on Phase 2 (input choice and assertion form moved). Whether SFT improves fixed-input output prediction is schema-dependent and unresolved (Phase 3A v2).

hypotheses.scope_note: input choice and assertion form moved under imitation; no value-prediction improvement is demonstrated. Causal support requires a Phase 4 arm.

evidence.why: not identifiable from retained outputs; needs a Phase 3 probe

Gate passed (answer rate 1.0 all levels; strict 1.0). C1 A4 7B-1.5B +24.79 [19.38, 30.42]; C2 A0 +11.46 [6.46, 16.67], Holm p<0.001 both. LIMITATION: a scale contrast (7B also differs in pretraining), not a manipulation of adapter capacity; LoRA rank / full fine-tuning untested.

hypotheses.name: dataset-distribution shift
hypotheses.claim: synthetic supervision does not represent the evaluated behaviour; gains stay on the training distribution
hypotheses.mediator: train-vs-held-out gap in P(correct oracle | disc) for the same checkpoint
supporting_signature: SFT raises P(correct oracle|disc) on training functions but not on held-out functions
weakening_signature: SFT does not raise P(correct oracle|disc) even on its own training functions

evidence.why: not identifiable from retained outputs; needs a Phase 3 probe
a train-only probe cannot support distribution shift; it can only weaken it (see protocol amendment 2 decision rules).

primary (prefill) schema, A0: SFT-base on exposed -1.67 [-7.6, 4.202], on literal SFT-target inputs -3.33 [-9.85, 3.252], unexposed +4.58 [-0.877, 10.081]; interaction -6.25 [-14.583, 1.667]. Rule 1: no improvement even on exposed training functions. SCHEMA SENSITIVITY: under the answer-schema control the exposed stratum is +5.00 [0.42, 9.836] (secondary, uncorrected). Distribution-shift arm untestable (no external cohort).
evidence.withdrawn_reason: exposure verdict violated the frozen schema-control rule (exposed stratum flips sign between schemas)

evidence.why: On exposed functions, the estimated SFT effect changes from -1.67 points under assertion-prefill to +5.00 points under the ANSWER schema. supporting_signature: Phase 2: the validity loss sits in parse/execute/contract stages
Probe B: constrained output recovers validity and Kill@8
weakening_signature: Phase 2: parse and execution are unchanged or better and the validity loss sits at the oracle stage

narrowed: progressive late-checkpoint degradation after step 100 is weakened. A rapid early SFT-induced capability shift or forgetting (steps 0-100) remains open.
